crossChecks.limitations: UN resolution uses recommends/requests, not a freestanding unlimited authorization for all future military actions. UK and US statements rely on the same UN resolution; provenance separate but source dependence declared.

payload.scope: 1953-06-26 to 1953-07-08 Robertson mission / armistice bargain
payload.provenance: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, FRUS 1952-1954 Korea XV Part 2
notes: d640: Eisenhower/Dulles accept joint withdrawal from political conference after 90 days if talks are exploited, but do not promise renewed war.
d642: U.S. aide-memoire conditions aid, 20-division support and treaty talks on ROK support for armistice and continued CINCUNC operational control.
d653: Dulles explicitly says the President cannot constitutionally pledge a future war without Congress.
d655: NSC 152nd meeting records U.S. post-armistice policy deliberation.
d659: State-JCS discussion records contingency planning to secure communications and POW camps against possible ROK non-cooperation.
d662: July 4 meeting shows Paik Tu-chin and Pyun Yong-tae as direct Korean negotiating participants; Pyun pressed treaty-ratification concerns.
d666: Clark records concrete military/economic pressure and contingency measures, including POW consolidation and slowing ROK force expansion.
d670: July 6 U.S. draft mutual defense pact ties response to constitutional processes.
d673-d674: NSC 154/1 and 157/1 separate immediate post-armistice tactics from longer-term Korea objectives.
d675: Clark plans renewed POW disposition discussions with Rhee.
d676-d677: July 7-8 aide-memoire exchange shows Korean conditions and Rhee's statement that he did not intend immediate ROK withdrawal from UNC operational control.

payload.scope: 1953-07-09 to 1953-08-07 armistice implementation, treaty drafting, reconstruction governance
payload.provenance: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, FRUS 1952-1954 Korea XV Part 2
researchLines: ROK written armistice non-obstruction commitment and its qualifications
ROK draft mutual defense treaty territorial scope
automatic response versus constitutional-process treaty language
Communist demand for ROK compliance guarantees
ROK request for post-conference military support
neutralization as U.S. internal bargaining concept
ROK local-cost burden for UN forces
ROK military-service chiefs in aid/force talks
civilian food relief and KCAC implementation

keyFindings.finding: Rhee's July 9 letter formally accepted non-obstruction of the armistice but retained a national-survival qualification; Robertson treated it as a major retreat from earlier demands, not an unconditional blank check.

The Korean draft treaty claimed lawful ROK jurisdiction to the Yalu/Tumen and proposed immediate mutual assistance language, demonstrating that the Korean draft was broader than the eventual constitutional-process formulation.

UNC could assure compliance of forces under its command but separately debated how far it could guarantee ROK governmental compliance and whether logistics could be cut off; force against ROK forces was explicitly not promised.
NSC 156/1 linked reconstruction and military expansion to post-armistice policy and recorded that implementation had been deferred while the Korean situation remained unclear.
On July 27 Rhee said he would cooperate with the armistice; the ROK did not sign the armistice, while UNC and Communist commanders did.
Post-armistice reconstruction became a governance dispute over CEB coordination, UN/US agency overlap, appropriations, exchange/conversion rates, local-cost burdens, and military-economic sequencing.
Paik Tu-chin, Pyun Yong-tae and Sohn Won-il participated as substantive Korean cabinet actors in August talks; Paik separately pressed economic-aid implementation and burden-sharing questions.

chronology.summary: 프랑스 대통령에게 보낸 서한에서 대한민국이 조직된 자치적 민주주의 국가라고 설명하고 국제적 승인을 요청했다.
임시의정원 계통의 심판 기록은 이승만을 임시대통령에서 면직한 사실과 탄핵 사유를 수록한다.
chronology.context: DB의 연감 표기에는 3월 11일 심판서와 그 근거로 기재된 3월 18일 탄핵안 사이에 날짜상 불일치가 보여 정확한 문서 성립 순서는 추가 대조가 필요하다.

chronology.summary: 독립촉성중앙협의회 결성 과정에서 여러 정치세력을 묶는 통합 활동에 참여하고 의장을 맡았다.
라디오 방송에서 신탁통치에 반대하고 완전한 독립을 요구했다.
미소공동위원회 재개와 통일정부 수립이 어렵다면 남쪽에서라도 임시정부 또는 위원회를 조직하는 방안을 언급했다.
chronology.context: 통일정부 가능성에 대한 비관과 소련군 철수 요구가 함께 제시된 상황발언으로 기록한다.

chronology.summary: 초대 대통령 취임선서에서 국헌 준수, 국민 복리 증진, 국가 보호와 대통령 직무의 성실한 수행을 선서했다.
국회가 국무총리 후보 인준을 부결한 뒤 그 이유가 명확해질 때까지 곧바로 다른 후보를 지명하기 어렵다는 취지의 담화를 발표했다.
정부의 공문서를 한글로 쓰는 것을 원칙으로 하는 한글전용 관련 법률이 공포되었다.
제주도지구에 계엄을 선포하는 대통령령 제31호가 공포되었다.
chronology.caveat: 진상조사보고서의 '최종 책임'은 위원회의 사후 조사 결론이다. 개별 학살 사건에 대한 직접 명령 여부와 전체 국가수반 책임은 구분해 저장한다.
chronology.context: 정부 진상조사보고서는 1948년 11월 계엄 이후 9연대의 중산간마을 강경 진압작전에서 대규모 희생이 집중됐다고 정리한다. 보고서는 집단 인명피해의 1차 책임을 현장 연대장들에게 두면서도, 대통령이 계엄령을 선포했고 1949년 1월 국무회의에서 제주·전남 사태를 '발근색원'하고 '가혹한 방법'으로 탄압할 필요를 언급한 사실을 들어 최종 책임을 대통령에게 귀속시키는 결론을 제시했다.

chronology.summary: 법률 제10호 국가보안법이 시행되었다.
정부 제주4·3 진상조사보고서는 1949년 1월 국무회의에서 이승만이 제주도·전남 사건의 여파를 완전히 제거하고 지방의 반도·절도 등을 가혹한 방법으로 탄압해 법의 존엄을 보일 필요가 있다는 취지로 발언했다고 확인했다.
chronology.caveat: 진상조사보고서가 인용한 국무회의 발언에 근거한 기록이다. 개별 작전·사건의 직접 명령과는 구분한다.

chronology.summary: 반민족행위처벌법 개정과 반민특위 특별경찰 문제에 관한 입장을 공개했다. 관련 사료 해제는 이승만이 특위의 수사 방식, 권력분립 및 치안 공백 문제를 제기했다고 정리한다.
반민특위 특별경찰대 해산 조치가 자신의 명령이었다는 취지로 밝혔다.
농지개혁법이 공포되었다. 이후 정부와 국회는 시행을 위한 수정·보완 절차를 이어갔다.
부산에서 한 전쟁 관련 방송에서 자신의 남하 이유와 한강 교량 폭파의 군사적 이유를 설명했다.
한국전쟁 발발 뒤 국민보도연맹원 등 요시찰인들이 경찰·CIC·헌병 등 국가기관에 의해 소집·연행·구금된 뒤 여러 지역에서 집단희생됐다.
chronology.context: 진실화해위원회는 이 사건이 정부 최상층부의 결정에 의해 이루어진 것으로 보인다고 판단하고 국가의 책임을 인정했으며, 이승만을 당시 행정부 수반이자 군 통수권자로서 책임이 있다고 평가했다.
chronology.caveat: 같은 진실규명 결정은 예비검속·사살명령이 정확히 누구에게서 언제 어떤 단위로 내려왔는지는 밝히지 못했다고 명시한다. 따라서 대통령의 구체적 사살명령을 확인된 사실로 기록하지 않는다.

chronology.summary: 6월 26일 밤 이승만은 무초 대사에게 각료들이 정부를 대전으로 이전하기로 결정했다고 알렸다.
무쵸 주한 미국대사는 이승만 대통령과 대부분의 각료가 서울 남쪽으로 출발했다고 미 국무부에 보고했다.
chronology.caveat: 외교문서에 기록된 이동 결정과 당시 시민 대상 대피 안내·방송 내용은 별개의 문제다. 대통령 이동의 시점·경로와 시민 공지 시간선을 섞지 않는다.
chronology.context: 6월 26일 자정 무초 대사와의 대화 기록에서 이승만은 각료들이 정부를 대전으로 옮기기로 결정했다고 알렸다. 6월 27일 오전 무초는 대통령과 대부분의 각료들이 서울 남쪽으로 떠났다고 보고했고, 다른 전문은 신성모가 이승만이 새벽 3시 진해로 향했으며 채병덕에게 군사 권한을 위임했다고 말했다고 기록한다.

chronology.summary: 국군 공병대가 한강인도교를 폭파했다.
chronology.caveat: 이승만의 후일 연설은 폭파의 군사적 목적을 설명하지만 누가 언제 폭파 명령을 내렸는지에 대한 명령계통을 직접 입증하지 않는다. 최창식의 후대 무죄는 최초 책임귀속이 잘못됐음을 보여주지만 곧바로 다른 특정 인물을 명령자로 확정하지 않는다.
chronology.context: 6월 28일 국군 공병대가 한강인도교를 폭파했다. 이승만은 이후 부산에서 한 연설에서 적군의 남하를 지연시키기 위해 교량을 폭파한 군사적 이유를 설명했다. 1950년 폭파 책임으로 최창식 대령이 사형됐으나 1962년 육군판결심사위원회가 무죄로 판단했고 1964년 법원에서 무죄가 확정됐다.

chronology.summary: 한국군에 대한 작전지휘권을 맥아더 유엔군사령관에게 이양하는 서한을 보냈다.
국민방위군의 식량·금전 관련 부정 보고에 대해 면밀히 조사하고 위법자를 법으로 다스리라고 지시한 대통령 문서가 남아 있다.
chronology.context: 1951년 1월 4일 대통령 명의 문서는 국민방위군의 식량·금전 부정 문제를 면밀히 조사하고 위법자를 법으로 다스리라고 지시한다. 이후 국회조사와 군법회의가 진행됐고 7월 김윤근 등 5명에게 사형이 선고됐다. 정치자금 관련 의혹은 국회에서도 별도로 공방·조사가 이어졌다.
chronology.caveat: 대통령의 부정 조사·처벌 지시는 직접 문서로 확인된다. 그러나 국민방위군 조직 창설·운영 실패, 예산 유용, 정치자금 의혹 각각에 대한 대통령의 사전 인지 범위는 같은 사실로 간주하지 않고 별도 추적한다.

chronology.summary: 거창사건과 관련해 제11사단장과 관련 대대장에 대한 징계를 지시하고 군 비행·범죄 감독 체계 개편을 지시한 대통령 문서가 남아 있다.
chronology.caveat: 사후 대통령 지시와 군법회의 기록은 확인된다. 사건 발생 전 작전명령 제5호가 대통령 또는 경무대까지 어떻게 보고·승인됐는지는 별도 입증이 필요하다.
chronology.context: 4월 30일 대통령 결재 지시문은 제11사단장과 관련 대대장 징계를 지시하고 군기·범죄 감독체계 개편을 요구한다. 이후 고등군법회의가 열려 작전명령 제5호, 현장 지휘, 조사단 방해 등이 쟁점이 됐고 연말 판정 이유서가 공개됐다.

chronology.summary: 대통령 선거 관련 성명에서 후보자 보호와 자유로운 투표권 보장을 강조하고, 자신이 선출되더라도 부정한 결속이나 운동의 결과여서는 안 된다는 취지를 밝혔다.
같은 선거 관련 성명에서 대통령직을 떠나 사인으로 살고 싶었다는 개인적 희망을 언급했으나 그 희망을 포기하게 됐다는 취지로 말했다.
chronology.caveat: 법적·정치적 불출마 공약으로 분류하지 않고 개인적 의사표현으로만 기록한다.

chronology.summary: 인접 해양에 대한 주권에 관한 대통령 선언을 발표했다. 이후 통상 '평화선' 또는 '이승만 라인'으로 불린다.
1952년 5월 24일 자정을 기해 부산과 경상남도·전라도 일부 지역에 계엄이 선포됐다. 이후 헌병이 야당계 국회의원들을 체포했고 국회·대통령 사이의 대통령 선출방식 및 개헌 갈등이 급격히 격화됐다.
chronology.context: 이승만은 5월 27일 계엄이 게릴라 활동과 폭력적 시위를 막고 질서를 유지하기 위해 필요했다고 공개적으로 정당화했다. 5월 28일과 31일 서한에서도 체포 의원들에게 공산주의 관련 혐의가 있어 합법적 조사와 공개재판을 거치겠다는 입장을 밝혔다. 반면 주한미대사관과 미 국무부 정보분석은 계엄·체포가 국회와 대통령의 권력투쟁 및 직선제 개헌 압박과 연결돼 있다고 평가했다.
chronology.caveat: 대통령 본인의 공개 설명과 미국 측 동시대 평가가 충돌한다. 미국 측의 '정족수 봉쇄'·'정치적 책략' 평가는 외교관·정보기관의 분석으로 표시하며, 대통령의 명시적 체포 지시 문서와 개별 의원 체포명령 계통은 별도 확인이 필요하다.

chronology.summary: 정부 담화에서 계엄이 게릴라 활동과 폭력적 시위를 막고 질서를 유지하기 위해 필요했다고 주장하면서, 헌법상 주권이 국민에게 있다는 조항도 인용했다.
이승만은 계엄령 선포를 게릴라 활동과 폭력적 시위로부터 평화와 질서를 지키기 위한 필요한 조치라고 공개적으로 설명했다.
chronology.context: 같은 성명은 정부가 취한 조치가 필요했고 오래전에 시행했어야 했다는 취지를 담았으며, 체포 관련 공산주의 연계 여부는 수사로 밝히겠다고 했다.

chronology.summary: 이승만은 정치분쟁 해결책으로 양원제와 대통령 직선제를 다시 제시하고, 국회가 대통령을 누구로 선출하든 국민의 뜻에 부응한 개헌을 먼저 통과시켜야 한다는 입장을 밝혔다.
제1차 개헌으로 대통령 선출 방식이 국회 간선제에서 국민 직선제로 변경됐다.
중국군 철수 등 특정 조건이 충족될 경우 통일 없는 휴전에도 응할 수 있다는 취지의 조건을 제시했다.
반공포로 석방을 실행하고 이에 관한 성명을 냈다. 이 조치는 진행 중인 휴전협상에서 중대한 한미·유엔군 갈등 요인이 됐다.
한미상호방위조약이 정식 서명됐다. 대통령기록관은 1953년 8월 가서명, 10월 정식 서명, 1954년 11월 발효의 흐름을 제시한다.
제2차 개헌이 공포됐다. 부칙은 당시 대통령에게 대통령 중임 제한 조항을 적용하지 않도록 했다.
chronology.context: 국사편찬위원회 헌정사 자료는 이 조항으로 이승만의 추가 출마가 가능해졌다고 정리한다.

chronology.summary: 정부는 공보실 발표를 통해 진보당의 정당 등록을 취소했다.
chronology.context: 정부는 진보당의 통일방안, 북한과의 접촉 의혹, 의회 침투 기도 등을 취소 사유로 제시했다. 이는 정부 조치로 확인되지만 대통령 개인이 취소 결정을 직접 지시한 문서는 현재 원장에 확보되지 않았다.

chronology.summary: 국가보안법 개정안이 국회에서 처리됐다. 처리 절차와 개정 내용은 당시 야당·언론 자유 문제와 함께 큰 정치쟁점이 됐다.
chronology.caveat: 입법행위 자체는 국회의 행위이므로 대통령 개인의 행위와 구분해 기록한다. 대통령의 직접 지시·관여는 별도 자료가 필요하다.

chronology.summary: 대법원은 진보당 사건에서 조봉암에 대한 사형판결을 유지했다. 다른 다수 진보당 간부에 대해서는 무죄가 선고됐다.
chronology.caveat: 정부가 진보당 등록을 취소한 사실과 조봉암에 대한 수사·재판·사형 집행은 확인되지만, 현재 확보한 자료만으로 이승만 개인이 재판부에 사형 판결을 지시했다고 기록하지 않는다. 직접 개입 여부는 별도 문서가 필요하다.
chronology.context: 진보당 사건 수사기록은 서울시경·육군 특무부대·검찰의 수사와 법원 공판으로 구성돼 있다. 미국 국무부는 1958~1959년 조봉암 사형 가능성에 반복적으로 우려를 표했고 한국 정부 유력인사에게 이를 전달하려 했다. 1959년 2월 대법원은 사형을 유지했고 7월 31일 형이 집행됐다.

chronology.summary: 정부가 군정법령 제88호를 근거로 경향신문 발행허가를 취소했다.
chronology.caveat: 폐간은 정부·공보실의 조치로 확인된다. 이승만 대통령 개인의 직접 명령 문서는 현재 확보하지 못했으므로 대통령 개인의 직접 지시로 단정하지 않는다.
chronology.context: 1959년 4월 30일 공보실은 군정법령 제88호를 근거로 경향신문 발행허가를 취소했다. 정부는 여러 기사·사설의 허위보도 또는 국가안보 관련 문제를 이유로 들었다. 5월 5일 미국측 외교문서는 한국 정부에 경향신문 폐간에 대한 우려가 전달된 상황을 기록한다.

chronology.summary: 조봉암에 대한 사형이 집행됐다.
제4대 정·부통령선거가 실시됐고 이후 부정선거로 인해 취소됐다.
chronology.context: 국가기록원의 수사·공판 기록은 최인규 등 행정부 핵심 인사의 부정선거 기획·집행을 담고 있다. 선거 전 주한미대사관은 경찰 동원과 행정부 차원의 불공정한 선거환경을 관찰했다고 보고했다. 반면 이승만은 4월 19일 매카나기 대사에게 선거부정 혐의를 몰랐다고 주장했다.
chronology.caveat: 선거부정의 조직적 실행과 대통령 개인의 사전 인지·승인은 별개의 입증 문제다. 현재 확보한 자료는 행정부 차원의 부정과 대통령의 사후 '몰랐다'는 주장을 동시에 보여주지만, 어느 쪽만으로 사전 인지 여부를 확정하지 않는다.

chronology.summary: 3·15 부정선거에 항의하는 대규모 시위가 이어졌고 정부는 비상계엄을 선포했다. 경찰 발포를 포함한 충돌로 다수의 사상자가 발생했다.
chronology.caveat: 이 동시대 외교문서는 이승만이 강경한 군중 통제 자체는 승인했다고 보고하지만 경찰의 구체적인 발포 명령을 직접 내렸다는 증거는 제시하지 않는다. 후대 재판 기록은 홍진기·곽영주·유충렬·백남규 등 구체적 책임자들의 지시·경비 체계를 다뤘으므로 대통령의 책임 범위와는 구분해 기록한다.
chronology.context: 4월 19일 밤 매카나기 대사는 이승만이 시위 규모와 원인을 충분히 파악하지 못한 것으로 보였다고 보고했다. 이승만은 군중 통제를 위한 '과감한 행동'을 승인한 것이 옳았다는 취지로 말하는 한편 학생들을 쏘고 싶지 않다고 말했다. 대사는 사망·중상 규모를 자신이 알려주기 전까지 이승만이 이를 몰랐다고 기록했다.

chronology.summary: 4월 19일 밤 매카나기 주한미대사와의 면담에서 이승만은 선거부정 혐의를 몰랐다고 주장했고, 시위대 통제를 위한 강한 조치를 승인한 것이 옳았다는 취지로 말하면서도 학생들을 쏘고 싶지는 않다고 말했다.
chronology.context: 매카나기는 이승만이 항쟁의 원인과 규모를 충분히 파악하지 못하고 있다고 평가했으며, 대사관이 파악한 사망·중상 규모를 전달했다. 홍진기 내무부 장관과 김정렬 국방부 장관도 배석했다.
chronology.caveat: 이는 미국 대사의 동시대 회담 보고다. 이승만의 '몰랐다'는 주장은 당사자 주장으로 보존하며 사실 여부는 별도 자료로 검증한다. 또한 강경한 군중 통제 승인과 구체적 경찰 발포 명령은 같은 사실로 취급하지 않는다.

chronology.summary: 하야 성명에서 국민이 원하면 대통령직에서 물러나고, 부정이 있었다고 알려진 선거를 다시 치르며, 국민이 원하면 내각책임제 개헌을 하겠다는 뜻을 밝혔다.
국회 결의에 따라 대통령직을 사임한다는 공식 사임서를 제출했다.
육군판결심사위원회가 1950년 한강인도교 폭파 책임으로 사형된 최창식 대령에게 12년 만에 무죄 판단을 내렸다.
chronology.context: 1964년 법원에서도 무죄가 확정됐다. 이는 당시 폭파 책임 귀속과 재판의 적정성을 재검토하게 하는 후대 자료다.

chronology.summary: 대법원 재심은 조봉암의 국가변란 목적 단체결성 및 간첩 혐의 등 주요 공소사실에 무죄를 선고했다.
chronology.context: 이 기록은 이승만 재임기에 발생한 사건을 후대의 법원이 다시 판단한 사후 검증 자료로 분리해 저장한다.

chronology.summary: 미국측 회의록은 한국측 참모진의 합의의사록 초안 검토 후에도 이승만이 직접 가조인하지 않았다고 기록한다. 미국측 보고이며 한국측 회의록 원본은 대기.
미국대사 Briggs는 이승만이 워싱턴 비준서 교환 지시와 합의의사록 수정 타협을 수락했다고 보고했다. 실제 한국측 지시 전보 원본은 미확보.
한국 공식 조약 제34호 공포문에 대통령 이승만과 국무총리겸 외무부장관 변영태·국방부장관 손원일이 표시된다. UNTS 워싱턴 비준서 교환 11/17과 한국 발효표기 11/18을 구별한다.
미국 NSC의 조건부 새 한국 지도부 지원 정책 승인. 이승만 직접명령이나 실제 교체작전 실행으로 해석하지 않음.
Stassen 회담에서 공매 지속·백두진 항의서 철회가 미측 보고에 기록됨. 한국측 회의록·이행 확인 필요.
미 외교문서는 양유찬 및 주일 김 공사에게 내린 군사원조·환율 관련 지시를 요약. 한국측 원지시 미확보.
UNCURK 8/9 5대1 민정이양 권고 후 UNC 사령관이 8/12 이승만에게 이양 준비를 통지. 실제 인계완료·영토 최종 귀속과 구분.
3개월 반NNIT 시위중단을 위해 최선을 다하겠다는 취지의 보고; 확정 보장 아님.
손원일 추가 군사원조 요청·백두진 5개년 재건 구상은 각료 제안이며 대통령 집행명령 아님.
미국 회고에 따르면 남측 NNIT 철수 완료; 이승만 직접 철수 명령으로 귀속 금지.
UNCURK A/2947 para11: 1954-11-15 and 11-17 UNC-administered northern areas civil administration handed over to ROK; not evidence of every local inventory transfer.
UNCURK A/2947 para33: National Assembly Jan22 adoption, Feb7 promulgation; Cabinet reorganization and redistribution of PM functions.
UNCURK para18: Rhee asked demonstrators to postpone deadline and avoid violence; this does not settle alleged earlier mobilization orders.

comparisonCandidates.rationale: 해방 직후의 정치세력 통합 노력과 1946년 남쪽 단독 임시정부 가능성 언급을 시간순으로 비교할 가치가 있다.
comparisonCandidates.changedConditions: 미소공동위원회 교착과 통일정부 수립 전망 악화가 핵심 조건 변화다.

comparisonCandidates.rationale: 국헌 준수 선서와 전시 계엄·국회의원 체포가 결합된 1952년 정치위기를 같은 헌정질서 축에서 검토한다.
comparisonCandidates.changedConditions: 한국전쟁 중이었고 정부는 게릴라·폭력·치안 문제를 계엄 사유로 제시했다.

comparisonCandidates.rationale: 정부가 국민주권을 인용하며 계엄을 정당화한 담화와, 같은 정치위기 뒤 대통령 직선제 개헌이 이루어진 과정을 함께 본다.
comparisonCandidates.changedConditions: 전시 비상상황, 국회와 행정부의 대통령 선출방식 갈등을 함께 검토해야 한다.

comparisonCandidates.rationale: 1952년 자유로운 투표와 부정한 선거운동 배제를 강조한 대통령 본인의 발언과 1960년 정부·여당의 부정선거 사건을 비교한다.
comparisonCandidates.changedConditions: 1960년 부정선거의 구체적인 기획자는 수사·재판 기록상 최인규 등으로 확인되며, 이승만 개인의 구체적 사전 지시·인지 범위는 별도로 입증해야 한다.

comparisonCandidates.rationale: 1952년 사인으로 돌아가고 싶었다는 개인적 의사표현과 1954년 현직 대통령에 대한 중임제한 예외를 포함한 개헌을 나란히 검토한다.
comparisonCandidates.changedConditions: 1952년 발언은 불출마 공약이 아니며, 1954년 개헌은 국회 의결을 거친 헌법 개정이므로 동일한 수준의 약속과 행동으로 취급해서는 안 된다.

comparisonCandidates.rationale: 헌법 준수 선서와 재임 중 현직 대통령에게 중임제한 예외를 둔 개헌을 비교한다.
comparisonCandidates.changedConditions: 합법적인 헌법개정 절차 자체는 기존 헌법 위반과 동일하지 않다. 개헌안 처리 절차와 정치적 압력 여부를 별도로 봐야 한다.

comparisonCandidates.rationale: 초기 국가보안 체제의 형성과 말기 언론 발행허가 취소를 안보와 시민적 자유의 긴장이라는 장기 정책축에서 추적한다.
comparisonCandidates.changedConditions: 각 조치의 법적 근거와 직접 의사결정자는 다르므로 대통령 개인의 단일 원칙으로 단순화하지 않는다.

comparisonCandidates.rationale: 재임기 진보당 사건의 확정판결·사형 집행과 2011년 재심 무죄를 연결해 후대 사법 검증 결과를 함께 보여준다.
comparisonCandidates.changedConditions: 2011년 재심은 후대의 법적 판단이며 당시 대통령의 구체적 재판 개입 여부와는 별개의 층위다.

continuityFindings.note: 해방 직후부터 재임 말기까지 강한 반공·안보 우선 기조가 여러 발언과 제도에서 반복된다. 세부 정책의 적법성·비례성 평가는 사건별로 분리한다.
1919년 외교 문서부터 정부수립 전후까지 독립국가의 국제승인 확보를 지속적으로 추구한 기록이 확인된다.
한국전쟁 중 미국·유엔의 군사원조에 크게 의존하면서도 휴전과 포로 문제에서는 미국과 충돌했고, 이후 상호방위조약 체결로 이어졌다.
한글 정책, 농지개혁, 정부 제도 정비 등 국가건설 관련 기록도 함께 보존해 정치적 갈등 기록만 과대표집하지 않도록 한다.

unresolvedLeads.question: 1925년 임시대통령 탄핵·심판서의 정확한 의결·작성·공표 일자와 절차를 원문별로 재구성할 것.
제주4·3 시기 대통령·국방부·경찰 지휘선과 개별 작전·민간인 희생 사이의 명령·보고 관계를 공식 진상보고서와 대통령기록으로 분해할 것.
unresolvedLeads.evidenceSoFar: 정부 진상조사보고서는 대통령의 계엄 선포와 1949년 1월 국무회의 강경 탄압 취지 발언을 확인하고, 현장 연대장들의 1차 책임과 대통령의 최종 책임을 구분해 결론냈다.
unresolvedLeads.remainingQuestion: 개별 초토화 작전·민간인 희생 사건의 작전명령과 경무대/국방부 보고 문서를 더 수집한다.

unresolvedLeads.question: 국민보도연맹 가입·관리 및 한국전쟁 초기 희생 사건에서 대통령의 직접 지시·보고·인지 여부를 진실화해위·군경 문서 중심으로 확인할 것.
unresolvedLeads.evidenceSoFar: 진실화해위원회가 국가기관의 전국적 실행과 국가책임, 이승만의 행정부 수반·군통수권자로서 책임을 판단했다.
unresolvedLeads.remainingQuestion: 위원회도 밝히지 못한 예비검속·사살명령의 최초 결정자·시점·명령단위를 군·경 원문에서 추가 추적한다.

unresolvedLeads.question: 한강교 폭파의 직접 명령·승인·보고 계통과 정부·군의 대피 공지 시간순서를 1차 자료로 재구성할 것.
unresolvedLeads.evidenceSoFar: 6/26 밤 정부 대전 이전 결정, 6/27 대통령·각료 이동, 신성모가 전한 채병덕 권한 위임, 6/28 공병대 교량 폭파, 이승만의 후일 군사적 목적 설명, 최창식의 1962·1964 무죄까지 연결됐다.
unresolvedLeads.remainingQuestion: 실제 폭파 명령 발신자·명령시각·채병덕-공병지휘선 및 시민 대피공지 시간선을 직접 작전명령·군사재판 기록으로 확인한다.

unresolvedLeads.question: 국민방위군 사건에서 대통령의 초기 인지 시점, 조사 지시 이후 후속 조치, 관련 정치자금 의혹을 판결·국회기록까지 연결할 것.

payload.scope: 1959 Seoul National University Graduate School of Public Administration founding-date semantics, institutional placement, first-cohort and research-office implementation

findings.claim: SNU GSPA's current official history describes the school as established in January 1959 by presidential decree inside the College of Law, then separated from the College of Law in March 1961.
findings.provenance: SNU GSPA official history and official brochure
findings.implication: The 1959 event should not be modeled as an already independent graduate-school bureaucracy; legal creation, host-unit placement and later administrative separation are distinct sub-events.

findings.claim: The same official history records the first 80 MPA graduates in March 1961.
findings.implication: The first-cohort graph can be anchored to a bounded population and a fixed graduation month rather than anecdotal alumni references alone.

findings.claim: SNU Korea Institute of Public Affairs states that its predecessor 조사연구실 began when GSPA was created on 1959-01-13 and was later renamed 행정조사연구소 under SNU Rule No. 95 on 1967-11-06.
findings.provenance: SNU Korea Institute of Public Affairs official history; KCI institutional registry independently converges on a 1959 조사연구실 start
findings.implication: The research-office layer is a distinct institutional sub-event attached to the founding network; exact first director, staffing, budget and internal order remain open.

findings.claim: SNU's 2014 official GSPA brochure explicitly cites the Education Act and Seoul National University Establishment Decree and gives 1959-01-13 as the establishment date.
findings.implication: 1959-01-13 is an institutional founding convention supported by SNU; it must be kept semantically separate from the previously recovered 1959-04-01 general effective date of Presidential Decree No. 1429.

findings.claim: Korea University's official profile of Paik Wan-ki independently records SNU undergraduate graduation in 1959 and SNU GSPA MPA completion in 1961.
findings.provenance: Korea University Institute for Government Studies official faculty profile
findings.implication: Paik is a strong first-cohort anchor but not proof of the complete roster.

findings.claim: SNU Archives biographical holdings show that a later GSPA dean served as Ministry of Education Higher Education Bureau director in 1960 and GSPA dean from 1962 to 1965.
findings.implication: The Ministry-SNU personnel bridge should be mined systematically; however this later career does not establish who routed the 1958-1959 proposal.

adversarial_checks: Do not collapse 1959-01-13 institutional founding convention into the decree's 1959-04-01 general effective date.
Do not infer that 조사연구실 existed as a legally separate research institute in January 1959 merely because later institutional histories date its origin there.
Do not infer the first GSPA dean from later deans or prominent founding professors.
Do not infer that all 80 first graduates entered on one identical date without the 1959 admission register.
Do not infer presidential policy origination from presidential-decree promulgation.
Do not infer Ministry proposal authorship from ministerial jurisdiction alone.
Do not treat a retrospective institutional founding date as equivalent to the first day of teaching.
Do not promote academic actors to politician registry without material public-office evidence.
Do not treat the 1961 administrative separation from Law College as a new legal founding of GSPA.
Do not resolve the 1958 No Yung-hee chronology anomaly without SNU personnel records.

payload.scope: SNU GSPA first-cohort reconstruction and the No Yung-hee 1958-08 chronology anomaly

findings.claim: SNU's official GSPA yearbook/history states that the school was established inside the College of Law in January 1959, produced its first 80 MPA graduates in March 1961, and was separated from the College of Law in the same month.
findings.implication: The first cohort is a bounded 80-person population and March 1961 graduation plus administrative separation remain distinct sub-events.

findings.claim: A 1969 article by Park Dong-seo in SNU GSPA's own Korean Journal of Public Administration explicitly reviews the preceding ten years of graduate education and divides the inquiry into admissions, curriculum and student guidance.
findings.provenance: SNU Open Repository and Archive, Park Dong-seo, '교육내용', 행정논총 7(1), 1969, pp.27-46
findings.implication: This is a high-value near-contemporaneous source for reconstructing the 1959 intake and curriculum even before the admission register is recovered. The PDF tables/pages should be extracted next.

findings.claim: Oh Seok-hong's 2009 autobiographical essay states that GSPA was founded in the year he graduated from SNU Law, that he entered when it was founded, and that he became a member of its first graduating class.
findings.provenance: SNU Emeritus Professors Association newsletter No.5 (2009), '학자의 생애', Oh Seok-hong
findings.implication: Oh Seok-hong is independently anchored as a first-cohort member by first-person testimony, but the complete roster still requires the official register.

findings.claim: Korea University's official profile records Paik Wan-ki graduating SNU Political Science in 1959 and SNU GSPA with an MPA in 1961.
findings.provenance: Korea University Institute for Government Studies official profile
findings.implication: Paik Wan-ki remains an independently verified first-cohort candidate.

findings.claim: Multiple biographical sources record Kang Shin-taek graduating SNU Political Science in 1959 and receiving an SNU public-administration master's degree in 1961.
findings.implication: Kang Shin-taek is a strong first-cohort candidate, but a primary SNU register is still needed before treating cohort membership as fully verified.

findings.claim: KRIHS's official 2021 exhibition booklet for No Yung-hee records his SNU GSPA professorship as beginning in August 1958, months before the January 1959 institutional founding convention.
findings.provenance: Korea Research Institute for Human Settlements official exhibition booklet, 2021
findings.implication: The chronology anomaly is now confirmed as an official-institution biography claim rather than a search-snippet artifact. It must remain CONFLICTED/NARROWED until an appointment order identifies the employing unit and retroactive labeling, if any.

findings.claim: No Yung-hee published a 1960 review through the SNU Law Research Institute, and SNU's repository classifies that item under the College of Law/Law School collection.
findings.provenance: SNU Open Repository and Archive, 법학 Vol.2 No.2 (1960)
findings.implication: This supplies a concrete Law College institutional trace close to the disputed period and strengthens the hypothesis that later biographies may have normalized an earlier Law College appointment into a GSPA career span. It does not itself prove the hypothesis.

findings.claim: A January 2026 obituary identifies Yu Hun as a founding GSPA professor, serving there from 1959 to 1994, and records that he passed the fifth higher civil-service examination in 1953.
findings.implication: Yu Hun is a founding faculty node with prior state-examination experience, but this alone does not make him a political actor or establish decree authorship.

Do not treat first-person first-cohort testimony as a substitute for the complete official roster.
Do not treat 1961 MPA dates alone as conclusive first-cohort proof where entry date is absent.

Do not collapse March 1961 first graduation and March 1961 separation into one event without exact dates/instruments.
Do not use later commemorative histories as substitutes for contemporaneous personnel, admissions, curriculum and organization records.

payload.scope: 1959 SNU GSPA first intake, founding chronology, and dean/actor network

findings.claim: A near-contemporaneous first-decade overview by Hahn-Been Lee states that GSPA was operationally established in April 1959 and enrolled a first class of 100 MPA candidates: about 40 daytime recent graduates and about 60 self-financing evening students drawn from middle/top civilian bureaucracy, government corporations and the armed forces.
findings.provenance: Hahn-Been Lee, 'The Graduate School of Public Administration, Seoul National University: An Overview of its First Decade', KJPA 7(1), 1969, pp.14-16; SNU repository PDF.
findings.implication: Pass 135's bounded 80 first-graduate population must not be conflated with the initial intake. The research graph now needs separate intake-1959 and graduation-1961 populations, with attrition/non-completion left open.

findings.claim: The same overview dates the SNU-University of Minnesota-ICA support contract to February 1957, the first group of eleven mainly Law College faculty departures to Minnesota to August 1957, the first Minnesota adviser arrival to March 1958, and contract termination to June 1962.
findings.provenance: Hahn-Been Lee, KJPA 7(1), 1969, citing Lloyd M. Short, Terminal Report, June 1962.
findings.implication: The institutional founding event should be decomposed into pre-founding technical-assistance, faculty-training, adviser-arrival, legal-establishment, operational-opening, first-intake and later separation sub-events.

findings.claim: SNU GSPA's current official history records January 1959 establishment by Presidential Decree and March 1961 delivery of the first MPA degrees to 80 graduates.
findings.implication: January 1959 legal establishment, April 1959 operational opening/first intake, and March 1961 first graduation are distinct chronology nodes rather than a single founding date.

findings.claim: An official SNU GSPA brochure gives the institution date as 1959-01-13 and lists Shin Tae-hwan as first dean from 1959-04-10 to 1960-09-19, Lee Byeong-do as acting dean from 1960-09-20 to 1961-03-31, and Lee Yong-hui as dean from 1961-04-01 to 1962-02-10.
findings.implication: The founding/first-graduation period has a concrete senior governance chain that should be represented as actor nodes and linked to the relevant institutional sub-events, without inferring policy authorship.

findings.claim: The same official dean table records Kim Jong-han (1962-02-11 to 1966-10-31), Hahn-Been Lee (1966-11-01 to 1970-09-09), Cho Seok-jun as acting dean (1970-09-10 to 1970-11-25), Kim Yun-tae (1970-11-26 to 1972-11-25), Park Dong-seo (1972-11-26 to 1976-11-25), and Yu Hun (1976-11-26 to 1982-12-05).
findings.implication: This creates a reusable institutional leadership spine for later politician/bureaucrat-network research and helps distinguish founding-era actors from later institutional leadership.

findings.claim: The Academy of Korean Studies encyclopedia identifies Hahn-Been Lee (李漢彬, 1926-2004) as a career official and educator: Education Minister's secretary from 1948, Planning Office budget chief, Finance Ministry budget director, 11th administrative and political vice-minister, diplomat, later SNU GSPA professor/dean, and in 1979-1980 Deputy Prime Minister and Economic Planning Board minister.
findings.implication: Unlike purely academic founding actors, Hahn-Been Lee clearly crosses the politician/senior-state-actor threshold and merits an independent stable politician/bureaucrat node if not already present.

findings.claim: SNU's university-wide history separately describes GSPA as becoming independent in the 1961-1973 professional-graduate-school expansion period.
findings.implication: This corroborates that 1959 establishment and 1961 independence/separation are different institutional acts; the exact March 1961 instrument remains an archival target.

adversarial_checks: Do not equate the 100-person April 1959 intake with the 80 March 1961 graduates.
Do not infer that the difference of roughly 20 represents dropouts without individual enrollment/degree records.
Do not collapse January 1959 legal establishment and April 1959 operational opening into a contradiction; preserve both with event semantics.
Do not infer that all approximately 60 evening students were civil servants; Lee explicitly includes government corporations and armed forces.
Do not infer that all eleven August 1957 trainees later became GSPA faculty without the Minnesota/ICA roster.
Do not infer that a dean authored the Presidential Decree or admissions policy solely from office tenure.
Do not treat the later official brochure as a substitute for contemporaneous appointment orders for dean start/end dates when exact legal authority matters.
Do not classify Shin Tae-hwan, Lee Byeong-do, Lee Yong-hui or Kim Jong-han as political actors merely from GSPA deanship; test their public-office careers independently.
Do not infer that Hahn-Been Lee participated in the 1959 founding merely because he later served as dean; his verified state career and later GSPA tenure must be temporally separated.
Do not silently harmonize the current GSPA January establishment wording with Lee's April operational wording; model legal and operational sub-events.

findings.claim: The first GSPA dean was not merely an academic actor. The Academy of Korean Studies records his later service as Minister of Reconstruction in 1961 and first Minister of National Unification, in addition to SNU presidency and economic-policy advisory roles.
findings.caution: The encyclopedia verifies ministerial offices but does not by itself establish his personal authorship of the 1959 GSPA decree, admissions policy, or curriculum. Those remain separate claims.

findings.claim: The acting GSPA dean in 1960-1961 also crossed the cabinet threshold: the Academy of Korean Studies records his appointment as Minister of Education when the post-April Revolution transitional cabinet was formed in 1960, and earlier four-year service as chair of the Ministry of National Defense war-history compilation committee during/after the Korean War.
findings.caution: His ministerial tenure overlaps the transition into his acting GSPA deanship only at the boundary; exact appointment orders must be used before asserting day-level overlap or causal responsibility.

findings.claim: A Korea Democracy Foundation chronology records that on 1960-06-23 Education Minister Lee Byeong-do publicly argued that the teachers union should be dissolved, while union representatives countered that organization was lawful and issued a resignation recommendation.
findings.caution: The chronology cites contemporary Chosun Ilbo and Dong-A Ilbo reports; those newspaper pages and ministry directives should be recovered before modeling the exact legal/administrative action.

findings.claim: The Academy of Korean Studies identifies Shin as a professor at SNU Law College, later SNU president, 1961 Reconstruction Minister, Bank of Korea monetary-policy committee member, and first National Unification Minister. This establishes a durable academic-state-policy bridge suitable for an independent annals node.

adversarial_checks: Do not infer that Shin Tae-hwan authored the January 1959 Presidential Decree solely because he was first dean.

Do not treat later biographical encyclopedias as substitutes for appointment orders when exact dates and legal authority are material.
Do not infer direct presidential instruction for either actor's later cabinet conduct without cabinet/presidential records.
Do not treat the Korea Democracy Foundation chronology as the underlying ministerial directive; recover the directive and contemporary press it cites.
Do not classify the teachers-union dispute as a GSPA event merely because Lee also served in GSPA governance; link through the person node, not institutional conflation.
Do not infer that all economic-policy advisory positions held by Shin carried executive decision authority.
Do not silently resolve variant Romanizations; retain aliases for retrieval.
Do not extend the verified ministerial threshold finding to the other GSPA deans without independent career evidence.

payload.scope: 1960 teachers-union dispute: split cabinet/ministry/labor actors and administrative actions

findings.claim: On 1960-06-23 Education Minister Lee Byeong-do publicly called for dissolution of teachers unions and threatened coercive measures against continued organization or membership; union representatives countered with a written rebuttal and resignation recommendation.
findings.caution: The chronology is an archival chronology citing contemporary Chosun Ilbo and Dong-A Ilbo; underlying newspaper pages and ministry records remain primary targets.

findings.claim: On 1960-05-07 Lee announced an education-policy response to post-April-Revolution campus rejection movements: students should avoid political involvement, educators should sever party ties, and a provisional Education Countermeasures Committee would be formed to pursue education-policy and legal reform.

The Education vice-minister publicly stated on 1960-05-09 that the ministry would neither block nor encourage formation of teachers unions; on 1960-07-01 he publicly explained the ministry's suspension of Kyungpook National University medical school after a professor-abduction/confinement incident.
sources: Korea Democracy Foundation Dictionary, 교원노조결성운동, https://dict.kdemo.or.kr/entry/94/
findings.caution: The May 9 statement is presently verified through the Foundation's synthesized dictionary entry; recover the cited contemporary press or ministry record.

findings.claim: As Health and Social Affairs vice-minister, Kim stated on 1960-06-18 that authorities would recognize unions upon notification; this position conflicted with the Education Ministry's anti-union line and preceded the Health and Social Affairs Ministry's June 22 request for a Justice Ministry legal interpretation.
findings.source: Korea Democracy Foundation Dictionary, 교원노조결성운동, https://dict.kdemo.or.kr/entry/94/
findings.caution: Exact wording, delegation of authority, and the June 22 inter-ministerial request require underlying ministry/press documents.

findings.claim: On 1960-06-29 the labor body formally accused Education Minister Lee Byeong-do of violating the Labor Union Act over interference with teachers' union organization and threatened employment disadvantages.
findings.caution: Recover the complaint itself, receiving prosecutor's-office record, and any disposition before asserting legal outcome.

adversarial_checks: Do not model the teachers-union dispute as a single Lee Byeong-do decision; Education, Health/Social Affairs, Justice, labor organizations and teacher organizations held distinguishable roles.
Do not equate a public statement with a written administrative order.
Do not infer the Justice Ministry's legal conclusion merely from the fact that Health/Social Affairs requested an interpretation.
Do not infer that the June 29 criminal complaint produced prosecution or conviction without disposition records.
Do not infer presidential direction from cabinet/ministry conduct during the transitional government without presidential/cabinet records.
Do not collapse public-school and private-school legal theories; the archival synthesis identifies different statutory arguments.
Do not infer that Lee Hang-nyeong's May 9 neutrality statement remained ministry policy after later June actions.
Do not infer that Kim Hak-muk personally authored the June 22 request to Justice; the current source attributes that action to the ministry.
Do not treat later biographical career summaries as proof of exact appointment dates where appointment instruments are available.
Do not merge the July 1 Kyungpook National University suspension with the teachers-union dispute; connect through education-administration actors only.

events.finding: KDemo daily archive identifies Lee Byeong-do press conference, threat of coercive response, and union rebuttal invoking Constitution article 13 and labor law.
Jo Il-mun stated that administrative litigation would follow concrete sanctions and that Civil Service Act article 37 should be amended as inconsistent with constitutional spirit.
Union and allied labor officials expressly invoked Labor Union Act article 6 as permitting organization and planned coordinated resistance to transfers.
Union statement specified 397 transfers and alleged Education Public Officials Act article 30 and Labor Union Act article 10 violations; treated as union legal claim, not adjudicated fact.
About 2,000 participants; Kang Gi-cheol threatened collective resignation/class refusal; legal and academic figures plus public-sector unions expressed support.
National Assembly debate exposed distinct legislative positions: outright opposition, pro-union questioning, and Oh Cheon-seok's organization-permitted/strike-right-denied government position.
Gyeongbuk union identified Kwak Tae-jin et al. as sponsors of a bill perceived as illegalizing teachers' unions and threatened fasting action.
Hundreds of regional teachers-union delegates demonstrated at the National Assembly against an illegalization provision; date discrepancy in contemporaneous reporting explicitly noted by archive.
KDemo dictionary says Education Ministry drafted a separate Teachers' Organization Bill and sent it to State Council Secretariat review; do not merge with Labor Union Act amendment.
Four education-establishment figures alleged violence/coercion by union members; preserved as attributed allegation pending police/school/union records.
ICFTU letter reportedly supported teachers' organizing rights under Korean and international law; classified as external advocacy, not domestic adjudication.
Union criticized police summons of delegates for building-entry allegations after Jan 16-17 sit-in; criminal-file target opened.
About 600 delegates demanded withdrawal of Two Evil Laws, release/reversal of measures against unionists, and issuance of union registration certificate.

adversarial_findings: The executive branch was not internally uniform in May-June 1960: Lee Hang-nyeong, Lee Byeong-do and Kim Hak-muk are reported with materially different positions.
The teachers' union itself cited multiple statutory bases at different stages; its legal claims must not be converted into court holdings.
The 397-transfer figure is stronger than generic 'about 400' reporting but still derives from union statement indexed from newspapers; original personnel orders remain required.
The September Labor Union Act amendment track and the Education Ministry Teachers' Organization Bill track are distinct and must not be collapsed.
The National Assembly debate demonstrates multiple individual legislators' positions, preventing attribution of a single view to 'the Assembly' or 'the Democratic Party'.
The October 19 allegations by Korean Education Association figures provide an adversarial source against a one-sided union narrative but remain allegations until independently corroborated.
ICFTU support establishes international advocacy/provenance, not binding interpretation of Korean law.
Later 1961 criminal prosecution cannot retroactively settle the legality of 1960 organizing.
The KDemo archive itself flags a date discrepancy for the Sept. 29 sit-in, so event dating retains provenance note.
The alleged 1959 Justice Ministry interpretation remains unresolved and cannot be inferred from the 1960 executive positions.

adversarial_checks: Do not infer that the State Council approved the Teachers' Organization Bill merely because it appears on the agenda.
Do not attribute the Education Ministry proposal personally to Oh Cheon-seok until the proposal file/minutes establish authorization or authorship.
Do not attribute the State Council's consideration personally to Chang Myon without minutes or instruction records.
Keep Kwak Tae-jin et al.'s Labor Union Act amendment and the Education Ministry Teachers' Organization Bill as distinct legislative tracks.
Test whether the simultaneously tabled Education Public Officials Act amendment was a companion measure or an unrelated technical amendment.
The KDemo statement that the Teachers' Organization Bill was eventually abandoned on 1961-02-12 still requires an official disposal record.
The KDemo characterization of the government's strategy as 'reformist co-optation' is historiographical interpretation, not a contemporaneous state document.
The union's characterization of the bills as illegalization or suppression remains an actor claim unless supported by bill text and legal effect.
The 1960-08-25 Daegu High Court result reported in later sources must be checked against the decision text before treating 'union legality' as the precise holding.
The 82-unit figure in KDemo's own July 17 summary strengthens the need to preserve the earlier 82/83 organizational-count conflict rather than silently choosing one.

payload.scope: Continue the 1960 teachers-union legislative/legal network from the State Council anchor, test contemporary press against later synthesis, and expand non-presidential actor/event leads without attributing institutional action to individuals absent primary proof.

confirmed_findings.finding: National Archives' official State Council agenda list places Education Ministry item 287 (교육공무원법 중 개정 법률(안), 3 pages) and item 288 (교직단체법(안), 15 pages) together at the 37th State Council meeting on 1960-10-08 in file BA0084253.
confirmed_findings.source: 국가기록원 국무회의 안건 목록집 I, p.234 / PDF page 16
confirmed_findings.open_question: Agenda presence does not establish disposition. Retrieve the bill texts and meeting minutes/result.

confirmed_findings.finding: Dong-A Ilbo's 1960-09-27 evening edition article index includes '法制室에 회부 敎職團體法案', independently narrowing the bill's administrative path to a Legal Office review stage immediately after the Education Ministry draft date reported by KDemo.
confirmed_findings.open_question: Open the page image/article text and identify whether 法制室 means the State Council Legal Office, the referral date, requested revisions, and responsible officials.

confirmed_findings.finding: KDemo states that the special committee reviewing the Labor Union Act amendment withdrew the amendment on 1960-09-29 after nationwide resistance. Contemporary KDemo event material independently records hundreds of regional teachers-union representatives demonstrating at the National Assembly against illegalization on 1960-09-29.
confirmed_findings.open_question: Retrieve the special committee minutes to identify the formal mover of withdrawal, vote/procedure, and whether the bill was withdrawn, rejected, or otherwise disposed.

confirmed_findings.finding: KDemo's event archive records a 1960-10-11 Daegu delegates meeting of the Gyeongbuk Teachers Union resolving to demand abandonment of the Teachers' Organization Bill and threatening a third hunger strike if it were submitted to the National Assembly.
confirmed_findings.open_question: Compare the resolution text with the State Council disposition to test whether pressure preceded a deferment/withdrawal or merely coincided with it.

confirmed_findings.finding: KDemo's event archive, citing Yeongnam Ilbo 1960-10-26, reports that the ICFTU sent the Korean teachers-union federation a letter supporting teachers' union-organizing rights under Korean constitutional/labor law and international law. This creates an external provenance line rather than a Korean-government or union-only claim.
confirmed_findings.open_question: Retrieve the original ICFTU letter or international archive copy, sender/signatory, date, legal authorities cited, and exact recipient organization name.

confirmed_findings.finding: Dong-A Ilbo's 1960-08-26 evening edition index reports that the House of Councillors resolved to question the teachers-union dispute (敎組紛糾質疑). This opens a second parliamentary chamber research line separate from the House of Representatives debate already tracked.
confirmed_findings.open_question: Retrieve the 1960-08-26 Councillors minutes, movers, questions, ministers answering, and any resolution text.

confirmed_findings.finding: Dong-A Ilbo 1960-08-25 records the newly formed Chang Myon cabinet's administrative reorganization and personnel context, including Education Minister Oh Cheon-seok and Justice Minister Cho Jae-cheon profiles, but the index alone does not establish their personal direction of the teachers-union legal actions.
confirmed_findings.open_question: Use cabinet minutes, ministry correspondence and parliamentary answers before assigning personal decision roles.

adversarial_checks: The State Council agenda proves tabling, not approval.
The Education Ministry as proposer does not prove Oh Cheon-seok personally drafted or ordered the bill.
The Chang Myon cabinet context does not prove Chang personally directed the bill.
The 1960-09-27 Legal Office referral suggests an administrative review chain but does not establish favorable legal approval.
KDemo's 1961-02-12 abandonment date still lacks an official disposal record.
The Labor Union Act amendment and Teachers' Organization Bill remain distinct legislative tracks.
The simultaneous Education Public Officials Act amendment cannot yet be labeled a companion bill.
The Daegu High Court decision cannot be summarized as a holding that the union itself was legal until the decision text is read.
The ICFTU letter is an external legal/political position, not binding Korean law.
The 1960-10-11 union threat may correlate with bill non-enactment but does not by itself prove causation.

execution_counts.counting_note: Search snippets were not counted as documents. The National Archives agenda PDF is counted once despite multiple searches/finds. payload.scope: Adversarially test the supposed terminal disposal of the 1960 Teachers' Organization Bill by tracing National Archives cabinet metadata after the May 16 coup; preserve bill-identity uncertainty and avoid equating same-title records without text comparison.

breakthrough.finding: The National Archives cabinet-record search independently indexes both '교육공무원법중 개정법률(제25회)' and '교직단체법(제25회)' with deliberation date 1961-06-21. This is after the May 16 coup and conflicts with treating the later-synthesis statement that the Chang Myon government's Teachers' Organization Bill was '폐기' on 1961-02-12 as the terminal end of the title/legislative lineage.
breakthrough.caution: The 1961 record does NOT yet prove that the June military-government bill is textually identical to, revived from, or legally continuous with the 1960-10-08 item 288. Same title plus the paired Education Public Officials Act amendment is a high-value continuity signal, not identity proof.

findings.claim: 1961-06-21 same-title pairing

findings.claim: 1961-02-12 terminal disposal

payload.scope: Extend the unresolved 1961-06-21 Teachers' Organization Bill lineage forward into the military government's later education legislation, without assuming textual continuity.

findings.claim: 1961-06-21 same-day paired education bills
findings.evidence: National Archives cabinet index page 144 lists no.1431 교육공무원법중 개정법률(제25회) and no.1433 교직단체법(제25회), both deliberated 1961-06-21; proposer fields are blank.

findings.claim: Later military-government education omnibus bill
findings.evidence: National Archives 국무회의 안건 목록집 I identifies 교육에 관한 임시특례법(안), proposer 문교부, BA0084271, item 20, 28 pages, production year 1961. National Archives subject registry identifies it as the 55th meeting item.

findings.claim: Promulgated terminal instrument
findings.evidence: National Law Information Center records 교육에관한임시특례법 as Law No.708, promulgated and effective 1961-09-01. National Archives separately registers Gazette No.2946, BA0188689.

findings.claim: The June Teachers' Organization Bill became or was absorbed into Law No.708
findings.evidence: Chronology and subject overlap create a strong successor-policy lead, but no clause-level evidence yet connects the 1961-06-21 교직단체법 to the later 교육에 관한 임시특례법. The latter must not be described as a renamed or merged bill without original-text comparison.

findings.claim: Military-government education control became broader than a teachers-organization-only question
findings.evidence: Law No.708 displaced conflicting provisions of the Education Act and Education Public Officials Act; official and institutional histories document abolition/suspension of education autonomy, centralized appointments, university restructuring, and later implementing rules. This broadens the research line from union status to system-wide education governance.

payload.scope: Test the unresolved relationship between the 1961 teachers-organization legislative line and promulgated Law No.708 by reading the official enactment/amendment reasons, without claiming textual lineage that has not been demonstrated.

findings.claim: Law No.708 directly addressed teacher labor activity
findings.evidence: The National Law Information Center's official enactment reason for 교육에관한임시특례법 (Law No.708, effective 1961-09-01) explicitly lists as item 7 a ban on teachers' labor movement and collective acts, together with a five-year reduction of teacher retirement age.
findings.significance: This closes the weaker Pass 148 formulation that the later omnibus act was only broadly adjacent to the teachers-union question. Law No.708 itself had a teacher-labor-control component. It still does not prove that the 1961-06-21 교직단체법 was renamed, merged, or textually absorbed into Law No.708.

findings.claim: Law No.708 was a broad education-governance instrument rather than a teachers-union-only statute
findings.evidence: The same official enactment reason enumerates a temporary Ministry reconstruction advisory body, school/department consolidation and enrollment adjustment powers, compulsory-education school exchange powers, two-year education colleges, altered education-superintendent appointment rules, stronger supervisory authority over university faculty appointment, teacher labor/collective-action prohibition and retirement-age reduction, suspension of vice-principal rules below universities, a national examination condition for bachelor's degrees, and criminal penalties for specified violations.

findings.claim: The original stated purpose included private-school supervision and restoration of educational order
findings.evidence: The official enactment reason says private schools were organized as Civil Act nonprofit corporations under insufficiently active state supervision and states an aim of eliminating corruption/pathologies, restoring normal national-education order, and improving quality.

findings.claim: Law No.708 remained static until repeal
findings.evidence: Official amendment history records amendments effective 1962-04-24 (Law 1062), 1962-09-24 (Law 1157), 1963-02-28 (Law 1285), and 1963-04-11 (Law 1319) before repeal.

findings.claim: Law No.708 was repealed immediately after civilian transition in 1963
findings.evidence: National Law Information Center records repeal by Law No.1466 dated 1963-12-05, effective 1964-01-01. The repeal reason states that the special measures were considered no longer necessary after educational order had largely recovered.

findings.claim: The 1961-06-21 교직단체법 became or was absorbed into Law No.708
findings.evidence: Law No.708's teacher-labor prohibition creates substantive policy overlap, but no original June bill text or disposition record has yet established textual or procedural lineage.

findings.claim: By the 2008/2011 statutory text Article 58(1)(4) no longer contained 노동운동, while Article 59 expressly recognized leave for a teacher serving as a full-time union official under the Teacher Union Act.

verified_findings.claim: The first local elections were held in two stages: city/eup/myeon councils on 1952-04-25 and provincial councils on 1952-05-10.
verified_findings.note: The NEC museum reports turnout of 80.2% city, 88.4% eup, 93.1% myeon, and 81.2% provincial.

verified_findings.claim: The 1952-05-10 provincial election created a large pool of independently identifiable local political actors; contemporary NIHK material preserves constituency-level names and votes for Busan/Gyeongnam and a separate Daegu/Gyeongbuk report.
verified_findings.note: Names are treated as local-politician candidates, not assumed to be national politicians.

verified_findings.claim: The executive constitutional program was already formalized before the May 1952 crisis: the 1951 government proposal combined direct presidential election and bicameralism, was rejected on 1952-01-18, and the government renewed its proposal in May.

Immediately before martial law, Rhee appointed Yi Pom-sok Interior Minister, Hong Pom-hui vice minister and Yun U-gyeong police chief; FRUS records the appointments and the subsequent martial-law declaration.
verified_findings.attribution_rule: Appointment and institutional command position do not by themselves prove authorship of each later arrest.

verified_findings.claim: The constitutional crisis involved distinct institutional actors rather than a president-only event: Cabinet, Interior Ministry, police, martial-law command, National Assembly factions, local representatives and foreign diplomatic observers all appear in separate records.

The 1952-07-04 amendment passed with 163 votes among 166 present and was promulgated 1952-07-07; its core effects included direct presidential election, bicameral legislature and a National Assembly no-confidence mechanism.
The first direct presidential election occurred 1952-08-05. Official archival election data report Rhee 5,238,769 votes, Cho Bong-am 797,504, Yi Si-yeong 764,715 and Sin Heung-u 219,696.

The vice-presidential contest was a separate multi-actor election. NIHK chronology reports Ham Tae-yeong 2,943,813, Yi Pom-sok 1,815,692, Cho Byeong-ok 575,260, Yi Gap-seong 500,927, Yi Yun-yeong 458,583, Jeon Jin-han 302,471, Baek Seong-uk 181,388 and Jeong Gi-won 164,907.

The June 25 assassination attempt should be modeled separately from the later government allegation of a political conspiracy. Contemporary reporting establishes Yu Si-tae's attempted shooting and immediate arrest; a July 3 Interior Minister statement names alleged associates, while the August court process supplies a later judicial layer.
verified_findings.attribution_rule: Government allegation is not silently converted into judicially established fact.

verified_findings.claim: The International Club case requires a correction layer: a later August 15 contemporary report says all 30 related persons received non-prosecution dispositions, despite earlier arrests/investigation.
verified_findings.note: Preserve arrest/investigation and prosecutorial disposition as different event states.

verified_findings.claim: The July 4 constitutional amendment and July 15 implementing legislation must remain distinct legal events; the police-produced attendance/quorum context precedes both.

Muccio's July 12 telegram describes the compromise as widely recognized as a Rhee victory while opposition and neutral leaders hoped martial law and coercive atmosphere would be relaxed. This is a contemporaneous diplomatic observation, not a legal finding.

A later State Department note attached to Rhee's June 25 letter states that martial law had been lifted and popular presidential elections had been held in a seemingly free and uneventful atmosphere by August 13. This is useful for transition chronology but must be checked against Korean election administration and opposition records.

US policy memoranda treated direct election as potentially legitimate in principle while objecting to coercion, martial law and destruction of Assembly independence. Therefore the research graph must separate constitutional-design preference from means used to obtain passage.

Rhee's June 5 assertion that nearly the entire voting population and all provincial legislatures supported dissolution remains an attributed political claim. No Korean local-council corpus was obtained in this pass to validate its breadth.

FRUS editors characterize the May-June 1952 episode as a constitutional struggle in which the US attempted to dissuade extralegal means and considered intervention, ultimately shelving intervention after Rhee prevailed. This editorial synthesis is not a substitute for Korean primary records.

adversarial_checks: Direct presidential election as a constitutional design cannot be equated with endorsement of coercive passage methods.
A contemporaneous US description of the August election as seemingly free and uneventful does not settle Korean opposition complaints or administrative irregularities.
Rhee's constitutional victory does not prove every Cabinet minister or police actor shared identical intent.
Ending political trials after amendment passage is chronology, not proof of an explicit bargain.
The 163-0-3 tally cannot be interpreted without the July 2 police attendance operation.
US intervention planning is evidence of US deliberation, not an executed regime-change operation.
US criticism of coercion does not imply US opposition to all direct-election proposals; d166 explicitly complicates that reading.
Rhee's nationwide-mandate assertion requires local Korean records rather than repetition through diplomatic correspondence.
Muccio's description of opposition fatalism is an observation by a foreign diplomat, not a complete census of Korean political opinion.
FRUS editorial synthesis must not silently replace missing Korean Cabinet, Assembly, police, court and election records.

Official/public-institution election sources identify four presidential candidates: Rhee Syngman, Cho Bong-am, Yi Si-yeong and Sin Hung-u. National Assembly-announced totals on August 13 were Rhee 5,238,769; Cho 797,504; Yi 764,715; Sin 219,696.

The 1952 election actor graph must include the vice-presidential contest independently. The National Assembly chronology records Ham Tae-yong 2,943,813; Yi Pom-sok 1,815,692; Cho Pyong-ok 575,260; Yi Gap-song 500,927; Yi Yun-yong 458,583; Chon Chin-han 302,471; Paek Song-uk 181,388; Chong Ki-won 164,907 among the reported totals.

Election-quality evidence is internally mixed and must remain decomposed: the US State Department later described the presidential election as seemingly free and uneventful, while NEC-commissioned scholarship discusses administrative intervention and the NIHK finding aid identifies observer photographs of anti-Cho material and damaged Cho campaign material. None alone proves nationwide uniform conditions.

The Liberal Party presidential and vice-presidential coalition was not a simple Rhee/Yi Pom-sok ticket. Muccio documented elite efforts against Yi before the election, and NEC-commissioned research records Rhee's support for independent Ham Tae-yong despite Yi being the Liberal Party vice-presidential candidate.

The Democratic Nationalist Party's October convention is evidence for the opposition's own retrospective interpretation of the election, including an allegation concerning Gwangju. It is not yet sufficient to create a verified Gwangju irregularity event without contemporaneous local administrative, police, press or court provenance.

payload.focus: Adversarial audit of the So Min-ho investigation committee's changing composition, plus stronger election/person provenance for investigator nodes

material_findings.finding: A contemporaneous Seoul Shinmun report dated 1952-04-27 says the National Assembly Interior Committee initially planned a five-member Suncheon investigation team: Jo Sun, Yu Hong, Lee Seok-gi, Kim Jeong-gi and Choi Ju-il.

The archival catalog for Investigation Report No.1 dated 1952-05-09 instead names six special investigators: Yu Hong, Kim Gwang-jun, Jo Sun, Kim Jeong-gi, Jo Jeong-hun and Lee Seok-gi. Choi Ju-il is absent, while Kim Gwang-jun and Jo Jeong-hun appear.

The five-person April 27 press list and six-person May 9 report list must not be flattened into one committee membership fact. The safest current model is preliminary/planned delegation versus later report-signing special investigation committee, pending the Assembly appointment resolution and original report signatures.

Choi Ju-il is independently anchored as a legislator associated with Gimje and appears in a December 1952 National Assembly investigation context. This makes him a legitimate politician-node candidate rather than a likely OCR/name error.

A 1948 UNTCOK candidate-list document also indexes Choi Ju-il, providing a pre-1952 political trace, but the exact 1948 constituency/result must be extracted before treating it as an elected-office role.

material_findings.finding: NIHK's constitutional-history DB identifies the exact Korean primary target for the Assembly release action as National Assembly Secretariat, 12th regular session stenographic record No.57, 1952-05-14. FRUS document 135 independently states that the Assembly acted on May 14 under Constitution Article 49.

A contemporaneous Chosun Ilbo report preserved by NIHK fixes physical release on 1952-05-19, followed by So Min-ho leaving prison at about 20:00, visiting the National Assembly secretariat, and returning home. This confirms a real gap between the May 14 Assembly action and May 19 physical release.

The current evidence does not yet identify the legal/custodial cause of the five-day gap. Later historical accounts attribute the release to Busan District Court judge An Yun-chul's suspension-of-detention decision after prosecutors did not execute the Assembly demand, but the original court order and prosecution/corrections paperwork remain the required primary targets.

Prosecutor General Han Kyok-man publicly announced on 1952-05-10 that the shooting was a simple individual criminal act without political character. His published charging narrative names So's Interior/Security Committee specialist Jeong Jin-dong and escorts Seo Won-ryong, Kim Cheo-jung and Lee Jong-seok, creating additional institutional actor leads independent of the later political interpretation of the case.

The April 25 Seoul Shinmun account and May 10 prosecution announcement conflict on important incident details, including reported shooting time (21:30 versus 20:40) and arrest framing. These should remain source-specific observations until Report Nos.1-3, police records and trial evidence are opened.

The April 25 contemporary report explicitly explains the Article 49 issue: a member could be arrested in flagrante, while release during session could follow an Assembly demand. This is useful contemporaneous legal framing but must still be checked against the 1948 constitutional text and Record No.57 debate.

NIHK modern-person data identifies Han Kyok-man 韓格晩 and preserves conflicting birth-date/year variants. His identity can be promoted as a verified institutional actor while the lifespan conflict remains explicit.

A modern judicial-history source identifies An Yun-chul 安潤出 as the judge who ordered suspension of detention and reports subsequent threats; another biographical source gives 1911-1994 and a post-liberation judicial career. Because the original 1952 order has not been opened, his event role is candidate/strong-lead rather than primary-verified.

FRUS document 138 independently establishes that the first government act under martial law was So Min-ho's re-arrest early May 25, followed by arrests of opposition legislators. This remains separate from the unresolved authorship of the Korean re-arrest order.

The archival catalog for NARA Box 15 confirms three distinct Korean investigation-report objects (Report No.1 committee investigation, No.2 So Min-ho statement, No.3 prosecution investigation), plus trial summary, photographs and scene/weapon photographs. These are the highest-value originals for separating committee findings, defendant claims and prosecution claims.

payload.focus: So Min-ho May 14-25 release/re-arrest chain: provenance-separated corroboration and public-reaction layer

material_findings.finding: NIHK constitutional-history synthesis cites National Assembly Secretariat, 12th regular session stenographic record No.57 (1952-05-14) for the Assembly action; US FRUS document 135 independently states the Assembly acted May 14 under Constitution Article 49. This is cross-provenance corroboration of the parliamentary act, while the stenographic record itself remains the preferred Korean primary original.

NIHK's preserved Chosun Ilbo report states that So Min-ho was physically released on May 19, left prison at about 20:00, stopped at the National Assembly secretariat, and returned home. The physical release therefore remains distinct from the May 14 Assembly resolution.

A separate contemporaneous Minju Sinbo item preserved by NIHK records an estimated 4,500-person rally in Busan on May 19 attacking the Assembly's So Min-ho release decision and using slogans calling him a murderer. This is evidence of organized public/political pressure around the release, not evidence that the slogans' factual accusations were judicial findings.

NIHK's FRUS-derived Korean database records that martial law was proclaimed effective at midnight May 24/25 for Busan, South Gyeongsang and parts of the Jeolla provinces, and identifies the immediately preceding appointments of Yi Pom Suk as Home Minister, Hong Pom-hui as vice minister, and Yun U-gyeong as police chief. These appointments should be modeled as institutional context rather than automatically as proof of authorship for later arrests.

The release-resolution controversy, the May 19 rally, physical release, martial-law proclamation, and May 25 re-arrest are analytically separate events. Collapsing them into a single 'Busan Political Crisis' node obscures which institution acted, when, and under what claimed authority.

material_findings.finding: The military layer of the Busan Political Crisis cannot be modeled as a single pro-government command chain. AKS biographical records identify Army Chief of Staff Lee Jong-chan as refusing a presidential troop-dispatch demand during the May 1952 crisis; AKS separately records Operations/Education Bureau chief Lee Yong-mun as joining the military-neutrality refusal and later being transferred. This creates an institutionally important opposed_by/refused_by branch inside the armed forces.

AKS's Lee Yong-mun entry ties the neutrality dispute to the May 26 detention of the National Assembly commuter vehicle and records Army Headquarters Directive No.217 ('To Army Soldiers') as the neutrality statement. The exact original directive remains the preferred primary target; later summaries must not substitute for the document text.

NIHK's June 17, 1952 reproduction of the US State Department OIR analysis reports that after the May 25 martial-law phase the Assembly was badly deprived of members through arrest, hiding, unknown whereabouts and boycott. This is a contemporaneous foreign analytical observation and should not be silently converted into a Korean judicial finding or exact arrest roster.

NIHK's overseas-archives catalog gives a precise NARA Box 15 target for the So Min-ho trial: Summary of the So Min Ho Trial, National Assembly special-investigation reports Nos.1-3, USIS courtroom photographs, June 20 trial photographs, and UN GA A/AC.39/INF.117. The catalog also names the six members of the May 9 special investigation committee: Yu Hong, Kim Gwang-jun, Jo Sun, Kim Jeong-gi, Jo Jeong-hun and Lee Seok-gi. These names are candidate political nodes, but committee membership still needs identity disambiguation before registry promotion.

Rhee's June 25 letter to Truman is preserved in the NIHK FRUS layer with provenance to the Truman Library White House central files. It explicitly presents Rhee's own defense that reports about the Busan disturbances were distorted. This is a high-value adversarial source because it preserves the principal actor's counter-narrative and must be stored as party assertion, not neutral adjudication.

Kim Seong-su's AKS biography records his May 29 resignation from the vice presidency in protest against the May 26 political crisis. This adds a constitutionally senior opposed_by actor and a distinct resignation sub-event rather than treating elite opposition as an undifferentiated bloc.

payload.focus: Busan Political Crisis: open Army HQ Directive No.217 and triangulate martial-law/troop-transfer command chain

material_findings.finding: The primary text of Army Headquarters Directive No.217, 'To Army Soldiers', is now directly opened in the National Institute of Korean History's Materials on Korean History. It is dated 1952-05-27, addressed from Army Headquarters in Daegu to all unit commanders, and signed by Army Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Lee Jong-chan. The text states that the armed forces are not subordinate to any institution or individual, must remain aloof from political affairs, and must preserve the military chain of command.

Directive 217 itself does not name President Rhee, the martial-law commander, or a specific troop-transfer request. Therefore it is evidence of Lee Jong-chan's institutional neutrality position, but it must not by itself be represented as a written refusal addressed to Rhee.

A May 27 FRUS telegram by Chargé Lightner records Gen. Van Fleet stating that neither he nor the ROK Army Chief of Staff had been informed or consulted in advance of the martial-law decision. Van Fleet also said he had advised Gen. Lee that he would not approve transfers of combat troops to Pusan because this would weaken the front.

The same May 27 telegram preserves Rhee's own account that the cabinet decided on martial law, that he suggested including Pusan, and that because of urgency written orders from the Chief of Staff were not obtained. Rhee said he telephoned Gen. Lee, after which the defense minister would issue the decree, Won Yong-deok would be appointed martial-law commander, and Won would take orders directly from the President. This is a principal-actor account recorded contemporaneously by US diplomats and materially narrows the formal command-chain question, while still requiring the Korean decree/order for domestic primary confirmation.

Lightner further recorded that Rhee accused Lee Jong-chan of involvement in a plot and displayed messages he said Lee had sent to Won and other officers, allegedly countermanding the prior oral understanding and directing the martial-law commander not to act except under Lee's instructions. Van Fleet defended Lee's loyalty and described his commitment to keeping the army out of internal politics. The alleged Lee-to-Won messages are now a concrete primary-document target and must not be treated as verified until recovered.

A later November 3 FRUS memorandum records Gen. Lemnitzer's retrospective account that Rhee demanded two Korean divisions be moved south to execute martial law, Van Fleet refused the two-division request, and one company was nevertheless authorized and apparently moved to Pusan. This complicates any simple claim that Lee Jong-chan alone blocked troop movement: the UN command layer also exercised operational control and refusal authority over combat-unit transfer.

The command graph should therefore distinguish at least four layers: Rhee/cabinet political decision; Defense Ministry decree channel; Won Yong-deok's martial-law command; and ROK Army/UNC operational-control constraints on combat troop movement. Direct presidential control over Won, as reported by Rhee to Van Fleet and Lightner, must not be collapsed into proof that every arrest or detention order personally originated with Rhee.

The May 28 National Assembly record reproduced by NIHK shows the Assembly passed a resolution demanding termination of martial law in Pusan by 96-3 with 139 present, after debate explicitly referring to the forced detention of more than forty legislators' vehicle. This independently anchors legislative institutional opposition and the Assembly's own legal response rather than relying solely on US reporting.

The May 30 FRUS telegram records the US demand that martial law be lifted in Pusan and notes UNCURK's recommendation that detained Assembly members be released so the legislature could function normally. Rhee replied that martial law would be lifted shortly while defending the arrests as an internal matter. This supplies an adversarial pairing of external institutional criticism and Rhee's counter-position in one contemporaneous record.

June 2-4 FRUS records show the crisis was not solely Rhee versus foreign actors: on June 3 Prime Minister Chang reported that most cabinet members refused to support Rhee's proposed dissolution of the National Assembly, and Rhee backed down at least temporarily after cabinet resistance and Truman's intervention. This creates a cabinet-level opposed_by branch that should be separately modeled.

payload.focus: Busan Political Crisis: domestic martial-law instruments, Won Yong-deok execution account, and personnel/security chain

material_findings.finding: A Korean contemporaneous record materially corrects the pass272 formulation that the Korean martial-law decree/appointment chain was still wholly pending. Defense Minister Shin Tae-young's May 24 statement says emergency martial law would take effect at 00:00 May 25, names Army Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Lee Jong-chan as martial-law commander, and separately appoints Maj. Gen. Won Yong-deok as Southern District martial-law commander responsible for the listed Gyeongsangnam-do districts including Pusan.

The same Korean record states the public rationale as renewed guerrilla activity and rear-area security after martial law had been broadly lifted for local elections. This is the government's stated rationale and must be modeled separately from the US Embassy's contemporaneous assessment that the Pusan inclusion was politically motivated.

Won Yong-deok's May 27 public statement supplies a Korean execution-side account of the May 26 National Assembly bus detention. Won said the bus failed to comply with a checkpoint at the temporary central government building, was towed to the 70th Military Police unit, occupants initially withheld identities, a roster was later made, the identities were reported upward, and after instructions they were allowed to act freely. This establishes a claimed reporting/instruction chain but does not identify who issued the decisive superior instruction.

Won's statement also repeats the official security rationale, citing guerrilla activity, alleged red-cell agitation in Pusan, and Pusan's logistics-base importance. Because this is the martial-law commander's own public defense, it is evidence of the government's stated justification, not independent proof that those conditions necessitated the Pusan political measures.

A May 24 Korean report confirms Yi Pom-sok was appointed State Council member and Home Minister replacing Chang Sok-yun on the eve of martial law. FRUS editorial reconstruction additionally identifies Hong Pom-hui as Vice Home Minister and Yun-Kyong as Chief of National Police immediately before proclamation. These appointments create a separate police/interior personnel branch that must not be collapsed into the Army martial-law chain.

FRUS editorial note identifies So Min-ho's May 25 arrest as the government's first act under martial law and says military police then attempted arrests of opposition assemblymen. This makes So's arrest and the later Assembly-bus detention distinct sub-events requiring distinct order attribution.

The National Assembly's May 28 resolution demanding termination of Pusan martial law passed 96-3 with 139 present. Debate by Kwak Sang-hoon explicitly invoked the detention of more than forty legislators' vehicle. This domestic legislative response independently contradicts any model in which the bus incident was institutionally treated as a routine checkpoint episode.

US contingency planning later contemplated an order to General Lee and the Second Logistic Command for protective surveillance, while explicitly preferring police/security control over UNC martial law. This reinforces that Lee Jong-chan's role must be separated across Korean legal command, UNC operational control, and hypothetical US/UNC protective measures.

material_findings.finding: The identity left unresolved in pass273 as FRUS 'Yun-Kyong' is now resolved to 윤우경 (尹宇景). The National Institute of Korean History's Korean rendering of the same FRUS editorial note explicitly names 윤우경 as the Chief of National Police appointed immediately before martial law. The Academy of Korean Studies biography independently identifies 윤우경, 1900-1995, as Seoul police chief and then Interior Ministry Chief of National Police in 1952.

Hong Pom-Hi is independently resolved to 홍범희. AKS gives the Hanja as 洪範憙, lifespan 1917-1972, and records a second term as Interior Vice Minister from May to July 1952. This corrects variant Hanja found in some later lists and supplies a biographical node beyond the FRUS romanization.

FRUS telegram 1170 records Rhee's own May 27 account that the cabinet had decided on martial law toward the end of the prior week; when approval was requested he agreed and personally suggested including Pusan. Rhee further said he telephoned Army Chief Lee Jong-chan, that the Defense Minister would issue the decree, Won Yong-deok would be appointed martial-law commander, and Won would take orders directly from the President. This is a contemporaneous diplomatic record of Rhee's own stated command arrangement and materially narrows the martial-law authority chain.

The same telegram records Van Fleet saying neither he nor ROK Army Chief Lee had been informed or consulted in advance of the decision to impose martial law. This creates a precise timing/provenance tension with Rhee's account: Lee may have been contacted only after the cabinet/presidential political decision, for implementation rather than prior consultation. It does not prove Lee participated in the decision to impose martial law.

Rhee showed Van Fleet papers he characterized as Lee's messages to Won and other officers countermanding the prior oral understanding and requiring the martial-law commander to take no action except under Lee's instructions. The papers themselves were not reproduced in the telegram. Their document numbers/originals are now a high-value lead because they could expose the exact conflict between presidential direct-command claims and Army chain-of-command claims.

Rhee told Van Fleet that Lee was implicated in a plot against him and might be removed; Van Fleet defended Lee's political neutrality and suggested Paik Sun-yop if replacement became unavoidable. This is evidence of a civil-military personnel conflict during the crisis, not proof that Lee joined a plot.

UNCURK report A/2187 independently records that So Min-ho was arrested by ROK military police after the May 25 martial-law declaration and transferred to court martial, and reproduces a public notice attributed to the Martial Law Commander. This supplies a UN provenance line separate from FRUS for the So arrest/court-martial sub-event.

FRUS telegram 1200 records the formal US position delivered May 30 that martial law should be lifted in Pusan because the CG EUSAK judged it unnecessary as a military necessity. Rhee replied it would be lifted shortly but defended action against an alleged internal conspiracy. This keeps the military-necessity assessment separate from Rhee's internal-security justification.

FRUS identifies telegram 1164 of May 26 as the UNCURK invitation that brought Van Fleet into the Pusan crisis discussion, and telegram 1196 of May 29 as containing the earlier wording of the US letter later delivered as telegram 1200. Even where the full unprinted telegrams are not online, their numbers, dates, subject role and archival file references are now concrete retrieval targets rather than generic leads.

FRUS editorial note on July 2-4, citing A/2187, records police 'guiding and escorting' absent Assembly members to the special session and the July 4 compromise amendment vote of 163-0 with 3 abstentions among 166 members. This is a later coercion/constitutional sub-event and should not be merged into the May 26 bus detention.
